title: Large language models for OCR in cultural heritage: a comparative study on Slovene Folkloristic texts
summary: Benchmarks six OCR routes - Tesseract alone, Tesseract with LLM post-correction, direct transcription by a general multimodal LLM, LLaMA 4 Maverick, Nanonets OCR-3, and Qwen-VL-OCR - against manually aligned ground truth on two Slovene heritage collections: uniformly typewritten folklore manuscripts and a visually heterogeneous children's magazine. Document-oriented and direct multimodal systems win on the clean typewritten material, while accuracy on the magazine tracks layout complexity more than model choice, so the authors argue for content-aware routing between strategies instead of one fixed pipeline. Scoring uses CER and WER plus sequence-based measures, which is the level of granularity needed to see whether errors are structural or character-level.
igbo_relevance: The undigitised Igbo print archive - mission-era orthographies, dense sub-dot and tone diacritics, mixed layouts - is the same problem class, and this gives both a shortlist of OCR routes to try first and a warning that per-collection CER on diacritic-bearing vowels, not a single corpus-level number, is what decides whether the text is usable as training data.

title: Seeking commonality while preserving diversity: A differential dual-path MoE solution for Multilingual Neural Machine Translation
summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts architecture for multilingual NMT built around two differentiated paths, one carrying structure shared across languages and one reserved for language-specific capacity, aimed squarely at the interference-versus-sharing tradeoff that governs many-to-many translation quality. OpenAlex has not indexed an abstract for this record, so it is logged as a lead: the routing scheme, expert budget, and language set still have to be read off the paper. It is tracked anyway because the shared/specific split is a core-task method question rather than a resource release.
igbo_relevance: Whether a low-resource language gains from or is drowned out by its high-resource neighbours in a massively multilingual model like NLLB-200 is decided by exactly this allocation, so the paper is a direct read on how to give Igbo dedicated capacity without losing cross-lingual transfer.

title: Normal-Anchored First-Order Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning based Whisper Fine-Tuning for Enhancing Fairness of Cleft Lip and Palate Speech Recognition
summary: Adapts Whisper to cleft lip and palate speech with a first-order meta-learning scheme in which plentiful typical speech anchors the inner loop while severity-stratified pathological speech drives the outer loop, so the objective optimises for robustness after adaptation rather than fit to whichever condition dominates the training mix. The authors ablate which Whisper encoder layers to unfreeze (0-5, 4-11, 6-11, 8-11) alongside decoder and projection-head tuning on two clinical corpora, and report that anchoring on typical speech alone is not sufficient - severe cases still degrade badly, with word error rates above 50% where typical speech sits near 4%. The honest reporting of that residual gap is more useful than the headline averages.
igbo_relevance: Igbo ASR faces the same data shape - one large anchor of abundant speech plus a small, internally heterogeneous target set spanning dialects and accents - so both the anchored meta-learning objective and the encoder-layer ablation are worth replicating directly when fine-tuning Whisper on the little transcribed Igbo audio that exists.
